one_line: Paramara king of Malwa, poet‑patron and warrior who expanded his realm across central India in the late 10th century.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, athletic and broad-shouldered with a disciplined, swordsman’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, sharp jawline and medium brown complexion; neatly trimmed moustache and short beard framing the mouth; dark, intense eyes with a calm, strategic gaze; default expression is composed and resolute, often with a faint knowing half‑smile.
appearance.hair: Black hair gathered into a short, high topknot at the back of the crown, sides and back neatly kept; a narrow gold circlet with a small central red gemstone sits low on the forehead, partially hidden by a thin maroon cloth band wrapped under it like a simple rajbandh.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length, long-sleeved angarakha-style tunic of rich deep green cotton with a wrapped front that ties on the right side, bordered with narrow gold piping and subtle block-printed floral motifs in a slightly darker green; over this is a fitted sleeveless quilted vest (padded coat) in muted maroon with horizontal stitch lines, functioning as light armor; his lower garment is a tightly wrapped dhoti in off‑white with a thin maroon stripe along the edge, pleated at the front and reaching just above the ankles, paired with leather strapped sandals; a broad cloth kamarbandh in mustard yellow wraps his waist, with the ends tucked and one short tail hanging slightly to the left; over his left shoulder he wears a diagonally draped shawl in dull indigo cotton with a subtle check pattern, practical and travel-worn; simple but dignified jewellery includes a pair of small gold hoop earrings, a single rudraksha bead necklace with a thin gold chain, and a copper signet ring on his right hand engraved with a stylised crest, all kept modest to emphasize his warrior‑scholar persona.
appearance.signature: A straight, slightly broad-bladed Indian sword of the period (early straight-formed proto-taluk sword), with a simple iron hilt and a disc pommel bound in dark leather, worn at his left hip in a plain brown leather scabbard, accompanied always by a compact palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with red string tucked at the front of his kamarbandh to signal his poet‑patron side.

ref_desc: Vakpati II Munja is a mid-30s, medium-brown, oval-faced king with a short beard, black hair in a topknot under a gold circlet, wearing a deep green angarakha, maroon quilted vest, off‑white dhoti, mustard sash and indigo shawl, carrying a straight sword and palm‑leaf manuscript bundle.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Vakpati II Munja as a historically grounded 10th‑century Paramara king of Malwa: a mid-30s athletic man with a medium brown complexion, oval face, straight nose, sharp jawline, dark intense eyes, and a neatly trimmed moustache with short beard, his black hair pulled into a short high topknot. On his forehead sits a narrow gold circlet with a small central red gemstone, partly under a thin maroon cloth band. Dress him in a knee-length, long-sleeved deep green cotton angarakha with a wrapped front and gold piping plus subtle darker green floral block-print patterns, over which he wears a fitted sleeveless maroon quilted vest with horizontal stitch lines as light armor. His lower garment is an off‑white tightly wrapped dhoti with a thin maroon border, pleated at the front and reaching above the ankles, paired with simple leather strapped sandals. Wrap a broad mustard yellow cloth kamarbandh around his waist with a short tail hanging slightly left, and drape a dull indigo checked cotton shawl diagonally over his left shoulder and across the torso like a practical travel shawl. Add small gold hoop earrings, a single rudraksha bead on a thin gold chain, and a copper signet ring on his right hand. At his left hip, show a straight, slightly broad-bladed early Indian sword in a plain brown leather scabbard with an iron hilt and disc pommel, while a compact palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with red string is tucked at the front of his kamarbandh to signal his scholar‑patron side. Use a palette dominated by deep green, maroon, off‑white, mustard yellow and dull indigo, and present him in neutral, front, side and back poses with a calm, resolute expression and subtle heroic bearing.
